title: Heuristic reading sprint: sessionization, context-switch cost, and compact KV ideas
content:
Quick summary / motivation:
- Trying to map practical heuristics for session boundaries and context re-use that are cheap to compute, robust across workloads, and friendly to continuous batching + prefix caching.
- Recent customer threads: chatbots with many short sessions interleaved across users -> cache thrashing + throughput drop. Need rules that reduce cold-starts without ballooning memory.

Top takeaways from papers/blogs skimmed this week:
1) Soft sessionization via recent-token embedding distance (paper: local-context drift): cheap to compute with incremental average embeddings per session but sensitive to prompt template changes. Works well for conversational threads with topical drift slower than token churn.
2) Time-decay heuristics (industry blog): TTL-based eviction but adaptive to request frequency gives best cost/latency tradeoff. Combine with LRU to avoid staleness.
3) Fragmented prefix stitching (research demo): store short canonical prefixes for common instructions, reconstruct full context by concatenating prefix IDs rather than full KV re-serialization. Avoids storing huge KV for repeated system prompts.

Brainstorm: practical heuristic set to try (cheap, stateless-ish or tiny per-session state)
- Session fingerprint: running average of last 32 token embeddings (64-bit sim hash) + last activity timestamp. On request, if sim_hash_near(session_fingerprint) and delta_t < adaptive_TTL then reuse prefix pointer else cold.
- Canonical-prefix table: hash(system_prompt + few-shot_templates) -> prefix_id. Maintain small hot table (1000 entries) per host. When session begins, check prefix_id; if match, mount cached KV fragment instead of building from scratch.
- Micro-eviction buckets by throughput tier: keep larger prefix cache for high-QPS customers only (paywall) to keep memory predictable.

Pseudo heuristic (rough):
- On request r from session s:
  1) compute sim_hash(r.last_32_embed)
  2) if sim_hash == s.fingerprint and now - s.last_active < TTL(user_tier) then route to fast-kv-path (reuse)
  3) else if canonical_prefix_id = canonical_table.lookup(r.system_prompt) then attempt stitching (mount small KV fragment)
  4) else cold path (build KV, consider async warming of similar sessions)

Open questions / pitfalls:
- embedding drift when prompts include user-specific tokens (names, timestamps) -> false negatives; need normalization heuristics.
- security: canonical_prefix ids must not leak other customers' private instruction content. Use per-tenant namespace or salted hashing.
- failure modes: stitching can produce output divergence vs full rebuild; need quality checks and fallback policy.
- operational cost: computing embeddings for every request increases cost; can we approximate fingerprint using hashed token n-grams? cheap but less robust.

Experiment ideas (MVPs):
- A/B: baseline = no-sessionization (current). Variant A: TTL+LRU; Variant B: sim-hash fingerprinting; Variant C: canonical-prefix stitching. Measure: token cost per successful reuse, 99th latency, error rate (regression on evaluation prompts).
- Microbench: synthetic churned sessions (100k sessions, 1k prefixes) to profile cache thrash and memory footprint.
- Small QA / hallucination test to detect divergence when using stitched KV vs full build (use static prompt set).

Metrics to collect (quick list):
- reuse_rate (per-session), reuse_success_quality_delta (BLEU / embedding similarity vs full build), average_tokens_saved, additional_compute_embeddings_cost, memory_bytes_per_prefix, false_negative_rate (should-be-reuse but cold), false_positive_rate (reused but quality degraded).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to Owen about existing canonical-prefix index prototype (PR referenced above).
- Try n-gram sim-hash fallback for customers where embedding compute is too expensive.
- Run a quick offline simulation using 7 days of anonymized session traces from dataset: TRACESET-2026-05 (Jira: INF-1987).
- Add a small test that replays sessions with and without normalization (strip dates, GUIDs) to see fingerprint stability.

References and quick links:
- Local-context drift paper (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12345 (note: re-check citation, I skimmed method section)
- Internal PR for prefix mounting: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/42
- Slack convo: #kv-cache-ops — thread 2026-05-18: "customer x saw 4x mem use on chat burst"

Loose notes / fragments (choppy things I might paste into a review):
- "We should treat prefix fragments like small artifacts: idempotent, verifiable, mountable."
- "Adaptive TTLs keyed by session QPS reduce thrash without hard guarantees — acceptable for hosted tier."
- "Embeddings for fingerprinting: use average of last N token embeddings from final layer; normalize common stopwords + dates."

Meeting prep bullets (for sync with solutions + SRE):
- one-sentence ask: validate 3 cheap heuristics offline and propose a canary for hosted (A/B) that reduces cold startups by 20% while keeping <1% quality regressions.
- data needed: 7-day anonymized session traces, per-request latency + model variant, memory profile during bursts.
- operations ask: is it safe to reserve small ephemerally persisted prefix table per host? cost estimate?

Links to follow-up tickets I will open:
- INF-2052: offline sim of fingerprint + TTL heuristics (dataset + script)
- INF-2053: canonical-prefix proto: privacy review (salted hashing + per-tenant namespace)
- INF-2054: stitch quality checks: lightweight divergence detector test harness

Random TODOs:
- strip placeholder tokens in sample sessions for experiments (dates/UUIDs)
- ask product for acceptable regression threshold (target <1% drift)

End notes: this is intentionally lightweight — want to iterate fast. Keep experiments small and measurable.
